text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.65% today, bouncing back after a sharp 3.9% drop on November 18th that followed geopolitical escalation in the Persian Gulf—Iran attacking U.S. military installations in Kuwait and the IEA warning that the Strait of Hormuz is no longer seen as a reliable energy corridor. The recovery today aligns with a modest stabilization in oil prices (US crude holding at $89.53/barrel) and suggests the initial shock from the conflict risks has begun to fade.

The bounce also comes as permitting reform legislation cleared the Senate, which would ease project development for both the energy and AI sectors. With data center electricity demand expected to double by 2030, there's potential long-term tailwind for oil and gas companies if the BAAJA bill becomes law—though it still needs House approval and the President's signature.
